module_title: Historical Movements in UP - Foundational Matrix (The Revolt of 1857)
introduction: Uttar Pradesh (then known as the North-Western Provinces and later United Provinces) was the absolute epicenter of the First War of Independence in 1857. At this foundational level, you must memorize the key centers of the revolt in UP, their Indian leaders, and the British officers who suppressed them.

core_concepts.title: The Outbreak of the Revolt
core_concepts.description:
- **Date & Location:** The revolt officially began on **May 10, 1857**, at the **Meerut Cantonment** by the sepoys of the 3rd Native Cavalry.
- **Immediate Cause:** Refusal to use the new Enfield rifle cartridges rumored to be greased with animal fat, ignited by the earlier martyrdom of Mangal Pandey (a native of Ballia, UP) in Barrackpore.

core_concepts.title: Major Epicenters and Leaders in UP
core_concepts.description:
- **Jhansi:** Led by Rani Lakshmibai (Suppressed by Gen. Hugh Rose).
- **Kanpur:** Led by Nana Saheb and Tatya Tope (Suppressed by Colin Campbell).
- **Lucknow (Awadh):** Led by Begum Hazrat Mahal and her son Birjis Qadr (Suppressed by Colin Campbell).
- **Allahabad (Prayagraj):** Led by Maulvi Liaquat Ali (Suppressed by Colonel Neill).
- **Bareilly:** Led by Khan Bahadur Khan (Suppressed by Colin Campbell).
- **Faizabad (Ayodhya):** Led by Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah (Famous for declaring 'Jihad' against the British).

important_entities.name: Meerut's 'Delhi Chalo' March
important_entities.significance: The rebel soldiers did not stay in Meerut. On the night of May 10, they marched toward Delhi, capturing it on May 11 and proclaiming the aging Mughal Emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar as the Emperor of India, giving the movement a pan-India political anchor.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often try to memorize a different British officer for every city, which leads to confusion. Remember a simple rule of thumb: The rebellion in the three biggest Awadh/Rohilkhand centers—**Kanpur, Lucknow, and Bareilly**—was ruthlessly suppressed by a single commander, **Sir Colin Campbell**.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Helps you instantly match Maulvi Liaquat 'Ali' as the leader of the 1857 revolt in Allahabad (Prayagraj).

exam_strategy_tips: In UP Police and UPPSC Prelims, direct 'Match the Following' questions are formulated using the City and the Leader. Ensure you know exactly who led the revolt in Faizabad (Ahmadullah) and Bareilly (Khan Bahadur Khan), as these are frequently tested.
